description: The chart compares the distribution of four categories across three difficulty levels labeled 'easy', 'medium', and 'hard' under Zero-Shot settings. Each of the three pie charts has four slices, representing the categories 'N+K+', 'N-K+', 'N-K-', and 'N+K-'. For the 'easy' category, the slices are 'N+K+' in teal at 55.4%, 'N-K+' in yellow at 38.3%, 'N+K-' in red at 1.7%, and 'N-K-' in orange at 4.6%. The 'medium' category shows a similar distribution with 'N+K+' at 58.8%, 'N-K+' at 35.4%, 'N-K-' at 4%, and 'N+K-' at 1.8%. In the 'hard' category, the proportions are 'N-K-' at 37.9%, 'N-K+' at 37.3%, 'N+K+' at 18.1%, and 'N+K-' at 6.7%. The chart includes a legend on the right side, and percentage labels are shown inside each slice. The slices are not visually emphasized or exploded. The categories are ordered by difficulty level, with the proportion of 'N+K+' decreasing and 'N-K-' increasing as the difficulty level increases.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of problem categories labeled as 'easy,' 'medium,' and 'hard' under Zero-Shot settings, with four segments in each chart. For the 'easy' category, the largest segment is 'N+K+' in teal, accounting for approximately 55.4%, followed by 'N−K+' in yellow at 38.3%. The 'medium' category shows a similar trend, with 'N+K+' comprising 58.8% and 'N−K+' at 35.4%. In the 'hard' category, 'N−K−' in orange is the largest segment at 47.9%, followed by 'N−K+' in yellow at 37.3%. Notably, the proportion of 'N+K−' in red remains consistent across all categories, stabilizing at around 1.7% for 'easy' and 'medium,' and increasing slightly to 6.7% for 'hard.' These charts highlight a decline in 'N+K+' as difficulty increases, while 'N−K−' exhibits a sharp rise in the 'hard' category.
